messages:
ada: quick heads-up — after the 2026-03-14 staging driver roll I see a tail perf hit on medium-length text-gen (seqlen ~400-900). p50 stable, p95 up ~35% in A100 pool. suspect KV churn + kernel picker flips.

kai: numbers? p50/p95/throughput?

ada: p50 ~ same, p95 +35% for seqlen 400-900, throughput down ~12% under steady-state traffic. only reproduces on our A100 cohort.

maria: which seqlen bins exactly? could be autotuner moving cohorts due to noisy signals.

ada: profiler snippet (simplified):
```
[prof] bin=384-512: prev kernel=matmul_v1 time=6.2ms kv_lookup=0.8ms
[prof] bin=384-512: new kernel=matmul_v2_alt time=9.5ms kv_lookup=1.0ms
```
Older runs favored matmul_v1 and lower wall time.

jon: kv_lookup changed too — we saw more misses. Any salt/keying changes in that deploy?

lee: we accidentally included the node runtime_id in the cache salt during the driver refactor to avoid cross-runtime collisions. That causes namespace fragmentation on roll.

maria: That explains both symptoms: 1) cold KV misses + increased lookup/miss cost, 2) autotuner sees noisy samples and flips kernel cohort for mid bins. Combined they blow tails.

deploy-bot: staging driver v1.18.2 deployed at 2026-03-14T03:12Z (rollout: 70% nodes)

ada: Proposed mitigation list: short: remove ephemeral runtime_id from salt and do a small canary rollback. medium: dual-namespace lazy-read remap (if miss in new, read old and repopulate). long: autotuner changes — add arch-aware priors, require N consecutive statistically significant wins before switching, and persist cohort state to KV metadata.

maria: For persistence, store a compact record per seqlen-bin: "cohort_id, wins, losses, last_change_ts, arch_hint". Keep binary-compact + TTL to avoid key blowup. Also add a small histogram of recent latencies to compute significance.

kai: Operators on private deployments will hate cache-breaking changes. Need a migration plan that does not force full rewarm. Dual-read remap + a mapping translation tool for operators is required.

jon: I'll own the lazy-read remap patch. Plan: on miss in new_ns, attempt read(old_ns) and if found, write into new_ns (hot-copy) and emit metric remap.hit. Also add a CI e2e that simulates rolling restarts to verify.

lee: I'll push a canary to revert runtime_id salt within 10m and monitor p95. If canary is clean we'll roll forward.

ada: Autotuner changes (maria): add stickiness window (e.g., require 5 consecutive wins and p<0.05) and persist cohort metadata under a single metadata key per model+arch. Also include arch_prior so H100/A100 have different defaults.

maria: will write short RFC for cohort persistence + metric sketch to detect false positives. Link when ready.

jon: small benchmark plan: synthetic workload with mixed seqlens + simulated node churn; measure how often autotuner flips under cold cache vs warmed. Will post results in thread.

ada: escalation criteria: if p95 >+20% after canary we rollback salt change. Tag me @ada on any alerts.

kai: good. please post canary dashboards to #eng-runtime and ping infra on rollback ready.

lee: starting canary revert in 5m.

ada: thanks. keep updates short. if anyone sees unexplained kernel flips or remap metrics, post here.

maria: adding perf test to CI to simulate cache namespace churn + autotuner noise. should catch regressions earlier. :thumbsup:
